_readme: Physical constants for GF180MCU's metal/oxide/substrate stack, used by inductor_spiral_generator.py's 3D FDTD geometry. Every value cites the exact file inside the eda-env-designer:gf180mcuD container's $PDK_ROOT it was read from -- confirmed by direct inspection, not from vendor documentation we don't have local access to. The one exception (substrate resistivity) is explicitly marked PLACEHOLDER.

z_start_m.source: libs.tech/klayout/tech/d25/gf180mcu.lyd25, sum of 'zstart' offsets up to Metal5 (860 + 1150*3 + 1450 nm)

areacap_to_substrate_aF_per_um2.source: libs.tech/magic/gf180mcuD.tech, 'defaultareacap allm5 metal5' (3 corner blocks) -- cross-validated against the d25 stack's physical oxide height via parallel-plate C=eps0*epsr(SiO2=3.9)/height =~ 6.0 aF/um^2, within ~5% of the measured value

sheet_resistance_ohm_per_sq.source: libs.tech/magic/gf180mcuD.tech, 'resist (allm4)/metal4' (3 corner blocks, same block grouping as metal5's own tt/ss/ff)

via4._readme: Metal4-to-Metal5 via, used by the center-tap crossunder (inductor_spiral_generator.py's add_crossunder()). No explicit z() entry for Via4 exists in gf180mcu.lyd25 (unlike Via2/Via3) -- it's the oxide gap between Metal4's top (z_start+thickness = 4.86um) and Metal5's own z_start (5.76um, see metal5.z_start_m above), i.e. height = 0.9um, taken directly from those two already-sourced numbers rather than a separate citation.
via4.modeling_note: This generator models the via4 connection as a SOLID conductive block spanning the Metal4-Metal5 gap at each crossunder endpoint (not a discrete via array) -- a deliberate v1 simplification. The per-via contact resistance found in gf180mcuD.tech ('contact via4' at 4500/15000/0 -- units and whether that third, ff-corner value of exactly 0 is a real physical number or a tech-file convention for 'not separately modeled' were NOT resolved) was judged not worth resolving for this generator's precision level, since even a modest real via array's effective resistance is expected to be small relative to the Metal4 trace's own resistance for the crossunder lengths involved here -- revisit if that assumption turns out to matter.

oxide.source: SiO2 relative permittivity -- standard material constant, not GF180MCU-specific

substrate.epsilon_r_source: silicon relative permittivity -- standard material constant, not GF180MCU-specific

resistivity_ohm_cm.source: PLACEHOLDER -- literature-typical bulk p-substrate value for a ~180nm process, NOT a real GF180MCU number. open_pdks deletes gf180mcu_fd_pr's raw source tree after `make install`, so this container has no volumetric substrate resistivity anywhere; not found either in the GF180MCU readthedocs Design Manual pages checked so far. Revisit before trusting absolute Q/SRF numbers from this generator -- see openems_inductor_status.md.

isosub_sheet_resistance_ohm_per_sq.source: libs.tech/magic/gf180mcuD.tech, 'resist (pwell,isosub)/well' -- real GF180MCU value (not corner-dependent), recorded here but not yet consumed by this generator's simple vertical-via ground model
